headline.title: Jersey Mike’s IPO illustrates how bad the AI hype has become
headline.summary: Jersey Mike's IPO documents unexpectedly referenced AI, highlighting the pervasive influence of artificial intelligence across various industries, even those seemingly unrelated to technology. This trend underscores the current hype surrounding AI, as companies feel compelled to incorporate it into their narratives.

articles.title: Meta quietly launches vibe-coded gaming app Pocket
articles.summary: Meta has launched Pocket, an experimental AI app that allows users to create and share interactive mini games through text prompts. The app is currently in a quiet rollout phase.

articles.title: OpenAI proposed donating 5% of its equity to a US sovereign wealth fund
articles.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has proposed donating 5% of the company's equity to a U.S. sovereign wealth fund, aiming to allow the public to benefit from the financial gains of the AI industry. This proposal has reignited discussions about public investment in AI advancements.

articles.title: Can Cursor Remain a Platform for OpenAI and Anthropic’s Models Inside SpaceX?
articles.summary: Cursor plans to maintain its platform for third-party AI models following its acquisition by SpaceX, aiming to facilitate collaboration between leading AI labs like OpenAI and Anthropic. This move could enhance the integration of advanced AI technologies within SpaceX's operations.

articles.title: Microsoft launches its own AI deployment company with $2.5 billion commitment
articles.summary: Microsoft has launched a new AI deployment company, committing $2.5 billion to the initiative. This move positions Microsoft alongside other tech giants like Amazon, OpenAI, and Anthropic in the AI sector.

articles.title: Achieving operational excellence with AI
articles.summary: The article discusses how frameworks like Lean Six Sigma and business process management (BPM) have historically provided structured approaches to improve operational efficiency. It highlights the integration of AI into these frameworks to enhance clarity and streamline complex business processes.

articles.title: OpenAI floats giving Trump administration 5 percent cut of AI boom
articles.summary: OpenAI is considering offering the US government a 5 percent ownership stake in the company to address tensions with the Trump administration and mitigate public concerns about AI. CEO Sam Altman believes this approach could help align public interests with the company's growth.

articles.title: Joyride Through July With 12 Games Coming to GeForce NOW
articles.summary: GeForce NOW is adding 12 new games in July, including Monopoly: Star Wars Heroes vs. Villains. The update aims to enhance the gaming experience for players during the summer season.

articles.title: Anthropic is discussing a new custom chip with Samsung
articles.summary: Anthropic is in talks with Samsung to develop a new custom chip for AI applications. This announcement follows OpenAI's recent partnership with Broadcom to create its own custom AI chip.

articles.title: Yep, we’re using OpenClaw to date now
articles.summary: Ben Guez has developed an automated script using OpenClaw and Claude code to facilitate dating, resulting in numerous potential international matches through Instagram. The tool leverages automation to enhance his dating prospects by managing direct messages.

articles.title: Teaching AI to run with the turbines
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence is increasingly being integrated into industrial sectors, where it plays a crucial role in managing physical infrastructure and ensuring operational safety. This shift highlights AI's potential beyond consumer applications, as it becomes essential for optimizing complex systems and maintaining continuity in various industries.

articles.title: Meta Is Charging a Subscription for Smart Glasses Features. Welcome to the New Era of Consumer Tech
articles.summary: Meta is introducing a subscription model for its smart glasses, requiring users to pay for "expanded access" to advanced features after purchasing the hardware. This shift marks a significant change in consumer technology, emphasizing ongoing costs for enhanced functionality.
